projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained 18-23 device count combined with zero camera motion at 11 PM strongly indicates a stationary, quiet evening (likely a movie night or settled guests) rather than active movement, confirming the household is safely occupied and winding down.

The sustained 18-21 device count with zero camera motion over four hours indicates the household is likely settled in for a quiet weekday evening, but the complete lack of movement from the children and active dogs warrants a quick wellness check to ensure no one is unresponsive.

The sustained 17-21 device count paired with zero motion or activity signals over four hours confirms all devices are stationary in a single zone, strongly indicating a large, sedentary gathering (likely guests or a media setup) rather than normal household movement. This warrants a quick check to ensure it is a planned event and not a network anomaly or unattended tech cluster.

The sustained 17-21 device count paired with zero camera motion and no signs of the active children or dogs moving around strongly indicates a network classification error rather than actual occupancy, highlighting a need to audit connected device profiles to prevent false presence alerts.

The sustained 17-21 'mobile' device count paired with zero camera motion over four hours strongly suggests the network scanner is misclassifying stationary IoT devices as mobile endpoints, explaining the inflated count for a four-person household and preventing unnecessary occupancy alerts.

The persistent 18-21 device count alongside zero camera motion over four hours strongly suggests a network scanning artifact or all occupants gathered in a single blind zone, warranting a quick verification of camera functionality and device filtering to rule out false presence alerts.

The sustained 18-20 device count alongside zero camera activity indicates a likely network classification error where stationary IoT devices are registering as mobile, or cameras are offline, which could disrupt presence-based automations. Verify camera status and device types to prevent false triggers.

The rapid increase of 6+ connected mobile devices between 14:55 and 15:41, paired with zero camera or motion activity, strongly suggests multiple unannounced visitors or contractors have arrived but are in camera blind spots or keeping devices in pockets/bags. This warrants a quick verification to ensure the household is aware of the guests and the home remains secure.

The persistent high device count (~14-17) paired with zero camera/motion activity indicates the presence data is dominated by stationary IoT devices rather than people, and the drop to 14 devices around 12:01 aligns with typical midday departures, confirming the house is effectively empty. This matters for automations like security or HVAC, as device count alone can mask an unoccupied state.

The stable presence count of ~15-16 devices combined with zero camera activity confirms the house is empty, indicating multiple personal devices were left behind rather than ongoing occupancy. This aligns with a typical Wednesday school/work departure.
